evals.name: full-greenfield-clinic
evals.prompt: I want to build a booking and billing system for a small private clinic in Phnom Penh. Patients book with a doctor, the clinic charges consultation plus any lab tests, and patients pay in USD or riel. Analyze, design and develop it.
evals.expected_output: Full mode. First turn delivers domain brief, BRs with evidence labels, scope, permissions and sensitive-data classification, open questions — then stops for correction before the full design.
assertions: Treats this as Full depth and delivers Phase 0-1 first rather than the entire design in one message
Every business rule has a BR-## ID and an evidence label; inferred/assumed rules carry H/M/L
No specific regulatory number or retention period is stated as [Known] without a source
Health data is classified and an audit requirement is stated
Includes a role x action permission matrix
Money handling addresses both KHR and USD and the stored exchange rate

evals.name: quick-class-diagram
evals.prompt: Draw me a class diagram for a library book lending system.
evals.expected_output: Quick mode. A Mermaid class diagram grounded by a short list of the rules behind its multiplicities. No SRS, no use-case catalog, no traceability matrix.
assertions: Output is dominated by the class diagram, not requirements documentation
Multiplicities are present and a short list of the rules they encode is given
Distinguishes Book (title) from Copy/Item (physical copy) or explicitly notes the choice
Does not produce a full requirements document or traceability matrix

evals.name: existing-codebase-anemic
evals.prompt: Here's our order module. Everything is in OrderService and the Order class just has getters and setters. Can you redesign the domain model? [paste: class Order { id; status: string; total: number; items: any[]; getters/setters } class OrderService { placeOrder(); cancelOrder(); applyDiscount(); markShipped(); calculateTotal(); }]
evals.expected_output: Existing-codebase entry. Reports the current model first (anemic, status string, float money), then proposes moving behavior into Order with a state machine and Money value object, citing GRASP.
assertions: Describes the existing model and its problems before proposing a new one
Identifies the anemic domain model by name
Replaces the status string with a state machine with defined transitions
Replaces number total with a Money value object
Justifies moving calculateTotal into Order with Information Expert

evals.name: rent-feature-addition
evals.prompt: Our rent system already has Tenant, Unit, Lease, Invoice. Add support for metered electricity and water billing per unit.
evals.expected_output: Feature-addition entry, Standard depth. Designs the delta: MeterReading, tariff, how utility line items join the invoice, edge cases like meter reset and missing readings.
assertions: Designs only the delta and reuses the existing classes rather than remodelling the system
Introduces a MeterReading concept and a tariff/rate concept
Covers at least two edge cases: missing reading, meter replacement/rollover, move-out mid-period
New rules have BR IDs with evidence labels
